words.form: drepr faður ... moðor ... systur ... vbota maðr

cognate: Kin noun + agent of *gʷʰen- 'slay': Ved. mātṛ-hán-, pitṛ-hán-, svasṛ-hán- ~ ON fǫður-bani, brǿðra banar, manns bani (bani < *gʷʰon-on-) ~ Gk πατρο-φονεύς ~ OIr guin athar (verbal noun guin < *gʷʰen-); kin nouns faðir/pitṛ, móðir/mātṛ, systir/svasṛ exact cognates.
drift_or_renewal: In the Norwegian law (AM 302/305) the verb is renewed (drepa) while the kin set is cognate; the *gʷʰen- agent noun survives in the same text type as bani (manns bani, AM 302 w603) and in homily/saga fǫðurbani, feðra banar.
shared_syntax: Enumeration of kin-objects (mother, father, sister...) of the killing, as a category of the worst, inexpiable offender: Ved. 'yo mātṛhā pitṛhā svasṛhā ye ca duṣkṛtaḥ'; ON 'ef maðr drepr faður sín eða móður ... eða systur, þá er hann óbótamaðr'; ON homily list of sinners 'feðra banar ok brǿðra'.
context: Both are catalogues of the gravest moral/legal offenders: AVP 19.46 lists matricide, patricide, sororicide among the duṣkṛt- 'evil-doers' whose stain is wiped off; the Landslög makes the killer of father, mother, brother, daughter or sister an óbótamaðr (beyond compensation), with the Homily Book's sinner-list feðra banar ok brǿðra. Gk πατροφονεύς (Od.) is the same agent formation for Orestes' target.
phrase: *ph2tr-/*meh2tr-/*swesr- + *gʷʰen- 'father-/mother-/sister-slayer' as the type of inexpiable offender
note: Kin-killing as the worst crime is near-universal and *gʷʰen- compounds are productive in Greek and Norse, so chance/parallel formation is a real alternative; the ON law is 13th c. and Christian-influenced. The claim rests on the cognate set of kin nouns + the same agent root in four branches, not on any one passage.

near_miss.lead: kin enumeration (father, mother, brother, son, daughter) in ON inheritance/wardship law ~ ORu. брат брату ... отьць сынови ... мати дъчери ~ Ved./Skt. mātā pitā bhrātā lists
near_miss.why_not: Cognate kinship nouns in lists are generic and unavoidable in inheritance law; no shared collocation beyond co-listing; contexts differ (inheritance order vs lament of social breakdown vs bridal/healing charms).

near_miss.lead: ON 'hæfir firirgort fé ok friði' (forfeits property and peace) ~ AVŚ 'paśūnām ca priyam dhāma' (fé~paśu, friðr~priya same root *preyH-)
near_miss.why_not: Syntax and sense differ (forfeiture formula vs 'dear abode of cattle'); fé ok friðr is a Germanic legal binomial; coincidence of roots only.

near_miss.lead: 'at guðs lǫgum ok manna' as gods-and-men merism ~ Ved. daivyā ... manuṣo
near_miss.why_not: ON phrase calques canon-law lex divina et humana; guð not cognate with deva; Vedic passage is not a merism of law.

near_miss.lead: 'þá er sól er í austri' (assembly time) ~ Ved. uṣā uvāsa
near_miss.why_not: Time reckoning by sun position is generic; no collocation shared (austr ~ uṣas root only).

near_miss.lead: 'um aldr ok um ævi' (for ever) binomial, ævi < *h2oyu-
near_miss.why_not: Only Germanic comparanda (OE ā/ealdor); partner MBh passage shares nothing; no cross-branch cognate binomial found.

near_miss.lead: 'láni heilu heim koma' (loan to come home whole)
near_miss.why_not: Catullus 'aduenit caelo' is unrelated; legal phrase about a borrowed object, no inherited collocation.

near_miss.lead: skull = sky (hauss kallaðr himinn) ~ Lucr. caput a caeli regionibus
near_miss.why_not: Lucretius' Religio showing her head from the sky is not the microcosmic equation; see search lead for the real comparandum.

near_miss.lead: 'kǫmr lífi í ljós' (born alive into the light)
near_miss.why_not: Slab partners irrelevant; best comparanda outside slab (search lead filed); metaphor is widespread.

search_lead.cognate: none lexically (haus / śiras-, himinn / dyaús are renewals); parallel is the cosmogonic homology head/skull -> sky in the dismemberment of the primeval being (Ymir ~ Puruṣa)
search_lead.argument: The skaldic kenning 'skull = sky' in the slab rests on the Ymir dismemberment (Grímn. 40-41, Vafþr. 21), which matches RV 10.90.14 head->sky, feet->earth item by item; a famous thematic parallel (Lincoln, Puhvel) but without cognate wording, so it is not phraseology in the strict sense.

search_lead.cognate: ON ljós ~ Lat. lūmen (*lewk-); Gk φάος renewal
search_lead.argument: ON law 'kǫmr lífi í ljós' (child born alive) ~ Ennian/Lucretian 'in luminis oras' (of birth) ~ Homeric birth goddess bringing the child 'to the light'. Birth as coming into light, with *lewk- in ON and Latin. Metaphor is widespread, so weak.

error.correct_reading: heili 'brain', gen. sg. (heila himintungl 'heaven-stars of the brain' = eyes)
error.evidence: Snorra Edda kenning context: eyes as sky-lights of the skull; 'heill' adj. gives no sense.

error.correct_reading: gler 'glass' belongs with *gʰel- 'to shine' (or is from Gmc *glaza-), not 'call'
mann, acc. sg. of maðr 'man' (veghr man 'kills a man')
error.evidence: object of veghr (= vegr, 3sg vega 'slay', left unmapped)
context 'veghr man eða væitir lemstra sor'

error.correct_reading: mann, acc. of maðr (giftingar mann 'marriage guardian')
manns, gen. sg. of maðr (manns bana 'a man's slayer')

error.evidence: exact cognate of ON systir, Lat. soror; mātṛ and pitṛ in the same line are mapped

note: Second reader on 30 flagged bundles (mostly Norwegian Landslög kin/inheritance clauses vs Vedic/Skt kin lists). One low-confidence claim (kin-noun + *gʷʰen- slayer as inexpiable offender); rest near-misses; two search leads; seven errors.
